title.narrative: South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation Power System Expansion Project

description.narrative: ADB assisted the Government of Nepal in increasing capacity of national power grid and enhancing renewable energy development. The South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation Power System Expansion Project is building more than 200 kilometers of power transmission lines, as well as substations, along Kali Gandaki corridor in the Himalayas and Marsyangdi-Kathmandu route. The project is also building or upgrading more than 1,000 kilometers of power distribution lines in the east, central, and west regions of the country. To bring affordable renewable energy to remote areas, the project is building small hydroelectric power plants, as well as mini-grid based solar and solar/wind hybrid energy systems.

Progress Toward Outcome: Status of targets for Outcome are:1. Power evacuation capacity from Kali Gandaki basin and Marsyangdi basin increased to 1,000 MW by 2025 (Baseline: 100 MW in 2013): Transmission lines planned in Kali Gandaki basin have been completed as planned while those in Marsyangdi basin have been partly completed. 2.Distribution capacities in identified areas increased to 316 MVA by 2025 (Baseline: 100 MVA in 2011): 240 MVA of distrubution capacity has been added. 3.30,500 additional households supplied by renewable energy in rural communities by 2025: 15,503 households have been supplied with renewable energy. 4. CO2 emissions reduced by 20,000 tons per year by 2025: It will be assessed approaching completion of project implementation.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Apr 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/44219/44219-014-apfs-en_19.pdf
Some results are in the Combined Resettlement Plan and Indigenous Peoples Plans | Feb 2021: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/44219/44219-014-remdp-en.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Mar 2017: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/44219/44219-014-iee-en_2.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Jan 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/44219/44219-014-smr-en_38.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: 1. Power transmission capacity increased: 216 km of 220 kV transmission line (Dana-Kusma, Kusma-New Butwal, New Butwal - Bardaghat, and Marsyangdi-Kathmandu) has been completed along with substations at Dana, Kusma, New Butwal, and Matatirtha. Reinforced grid substations at Dhalkebar, Lahan, Damauli, Baneshwor, Banepa, New Kawasoti, Butwal, Bharatpur, Butwal, and Gandak are in operation.
2.Power distribution network improved: 240 MVA of distribution capacity has been added through 20 distribution substations. Construction of 5 distribution substations are ongoing. Dhalkebar-Mujeliya 33 kV line has been upgraded. About 482km of 33kV, 11kV, and 400V distribution lines have been installed and charged at various locations.
3.Mini-grid-based renewable energy systems in off-grid areas increased: 9 Wind/Solar Mini Grid Systems of 565 kWp completed. Five MHPs of 2,098 kW are completed and 2 for 1,496 kW are under construction.
4.Capacity development support provided to NEA and AEPC. Project management monitoring system developed in NEA and AEPC. More than 20 persons trained in GESI-based community participation and management of energy systems. Feasibility study for Chisapani (Kailali) met mast station had been done, approved by AEPC and implementation of the system completed. NEA board approved the master plan on 27 October 2021.
5. Utility scale solar photovoltaic projects developed: 11 MWp solar PV capacity has been added under this output. Implementation of solar PV power plants with battery energy storage system (BESS) have started in Mugu, Jumla, Humla, and Dolpa.
TA 8678: 86% disbursed as of 17 Jul 2025
